keyVerseText: And Shallum begat Jekamiah, and Jekamiah begat Elishama.
rootMeaning: The name יְקַמְיָה (Yᵉqamyâh) originates from the Hebrew root קוּם (qûwm), meaning to rise, stand, or establish, combined with יָהּ (Yah), a shortened form of the divine name Yahweh. Thus, the literal meaning is 'Yahweh will raise' or 'Jehovah raises.' This etymology conveys a sense of divine action—God as the one who lifts up or establishes, which goes beyond a mere personal name to reflect God's sustaining and elevating power.
usageInScripture: The name יְקַמְיָה appears three times in Scripture, always as a proper masculine name referring to two distinct individuals within Israel's history: one a descendant of Judah and another a descendant of David. It is translated primarily as 'Jekamiah' twice and once as 'Jecamiah,' showing minor variation but consistent recognition as a personal name tied to the meaning 'Jehovah raises.' This consistency highlights the importance of divine empowerment associated with these individuals' identities.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יְקַמְיָה as 'Jehovah raises' reminds believers that God is the ultimate source of elevation and restoration, especially within the covenant community of Israel. The name reflects a theological truth that God sustains His people and raises up leaders and descendants according to His sovereign will. For Christians, this points forward to Christ, the one whom God has raised as King and Savior, affirming that all true authority and life come from the Lord. It encourages faith in God's power to uphold His promises and to raise His people from failure or exile.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 2:41, 'And Shallum begat Jekamiah, and Jekamiah begat Elishama,' the mention of Jekamiah highlights a link in the genealogical line of Judah. The name 'Jekamiah' here is not just a marker of ancestry but a reminder that God is actively involved in raising and preserving His chosen line. This underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining His covenant through successive generations, encouraging trust in His ongoing work in history.
